claims.statement: The distribution pattern of many individual particles mimics the diffraction pattern produced by waves.
The double-slit experiment was seen as a demonstration of the wave nature of light.
The source says that the observation of the same type of interference pattern in experiments using matter demonstrates that all matter possesses wave characteristics.
When the source intensity is reduced, the interference pattern builds up one particle at a time, including photons or electrons.
Wave–particle duality says that neither the classical concept of a particle nor the classical concept of a wave can fully describe quantum-scale objects, including photons and matter.
In the double-slit experiment, the quantum system acts as a wave when passing through the double slits and as a particle when detected.

relationships.statement: The double-slit experiment produces an interference pattern.
Wave–particle duality is an example of the principle of complementarity.
Variations of the double-slit experiment using electrons and atoms produce the same type of interference pattern.
